sources.entry: OpenRouteService - Route service with directions, isochrones, time-distance matrix, route optimization, etc. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/Java

summary.one_liner: Openrouteservice is a Java routing service, built on a forked GraphHopper 4.0, that provides directions, isochrones, matrix, snapping and export APIs using OpenStreetMap data.
summary.what_it_does: Openrouteservice is a self-hostable routing backend written in Java that uses a forked and edited version of GraphHopper 4.0. It offers a directions service for several transport modes, an isochrones service for reachable areas from given locations, and a matrix service for one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many time and distance matrices. It also provides a snapping service that moves coordinates onto the road network and an export service that exports the base graph for each transport mode. Health and status endpoints are available when running your own instance, but not on the public live API. The README says the install is Docker-based: it creates data directories and starts the service with docker compose, using a sample OSM file for Heidelberg, Germany. The endpoints are served on port 8080.
use_cases: build travel time or distance matrices
snap GPS coordinates to the road network
export a road graph for a transport mode
how_to_run: mkdir -p ors-docker/config ors-docker/elevation_cache ors-docker/graphs ors-docker/files ors-docker/logs
Change to the install directory and obtain the docker compose file (the README's wget line has no URL)
notable: Directions, isochrones, matrix, snapping and export services in one backend
Built on a forked and edited GraphHopper 4.0
Docker-based install with a sample Heidelberg OSM dataset
Companion HeiGIT services (openpoiservice, openelevationservice, Pelias, VROOM) are separate projects, not part of this repo
caveats: Health and Status endpoints are not available on the public live API; only on self-run instances
The README's download step (wget) is incomplete, so the compose file location must be found elsewhere
Nightly main-branch builds are for experienced users only; release versions are recommended
